Case study · UX/UI design

Neurowave: sleep support for neurodivergent minds.

A sleep app concept that uses wearable data for personal insights and AI-generated sleep sounds tailored to each person's sensory needs and routines.

ProjectNeurowave sleep app
RoleProduct design
WhenSeptember 2024
ScopeResearch · Personas · Competitive analysis · Visual identity · Mid-fidelity wireframes

The brief

Help neurodivergent people understand their sleep, and give them what they need to sleep better.

The research looks at their sensory sensitivities, sleep patterns and daily routines. Restless nights often start a downward spiral, so spotting the triggers early gives people a chance to break the cycle before it sets in.

Research

What disrupts sleep

  • Environmental: sounds, smells, uncomfortable textures
  • Situational: routine changes, illness, work schedule
  • Social: housemates, partners, social events
  • Emotional: anxiety, sadness, stress

Habit loops we designed around

  • Sensory calming routine: dimmed light, soothing music, white noise, deep breathing
  • Visual schedule for the bedtime routine
  • Melatonin tracker linked to sleep quality
  • Anxiety management: guided relaxation, mindfulness, CBT for bedtime anxiety
  • Optimising the sleep environment: light, temperature, noise, sensory-friendly bedding
  • Flexible sleep scheduling with reminders

Competitive analysis

We compared five existing products, from sleep apps to wearables, on strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats.

Wellness

Room to add wellness tools for a more holistic approach.

Personalisation

AI can personalise sleep stories, sounds and meditations to each person.

Reach and smart home

Support more than one wearable platform and connect to smart home devices.

Personas

Three people with different sleep struggles: Luka, a stressed designer whose anxiety worsens in unfamiliar places; Kreda, a student with irregular sleep and sensitivity to sound and light; and Sheniqua, a mother looking for a quick way to manage her child's sensory needs and sleep.

Visual identity

Calm, dark and soft. The type is Plus Jakarta Sans, and the palette runs from deep midnight to gentle lilac.
